ad: The coat of arms on Andorra's flag includes two red cows, a symbol borrowed from the neighboring French region of Béarn.
ae: The flag of the United Arab Emirates was designed in 1971 by Abdullah Mohammed Al Maainah, who was just 19 years old at the time.
af: Afghanistan changed its national flag more times in the 20th century than almost any other country, with well over a dozen designs.
ag: Antigua and Barbuda's rising-sun flag was designed by artist Reginald Samuel, whose entry beat more than 600 others in a 1960s competition.
al: The black double-headed eagle on Albania's flag is linked to Skanderbeg, the 15th-century national hero who used it on his seal.
am: Armenia's red, blue and orange tricolor was first used by the republic of 1918-1920 and was brought back as the national flag in 1990.
ao: Angola's flag shows half a cogwheel crossed by a machete, standing for industrial workers and farmers, beneath a five-pointed star.
ar: Argentina's blue and white flag was created by Manuel Belgrano in 1812, and the golden Sun of May was added to it in 1818.
at: Austria's red-white-red is one of the oldest national symbols; legend links it to Duke Leopold V's blood-soaked white tunic in 1191.
au: Australia's flag came from a 1901 competition with over 32,000 entries, and its big seven-pointed star stands for the states and territories.
az: Azerbaijan's flag was first adopted in 1918 and brought back in 1991; its colors are often said to mean Turkic heritage, progress and Islam.
ba: On the flag of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the stars at the top and bottom are cut in half to suggest a row of stars that goes on forever.
bb: The broken trident on Barbados's flag stands for the island's break from its colonial past; the old colonial badge showed a whole trident.
bd: The red disc on Bangladesh's flag sits slightly toward the pole, so that it looks centered when the flag is flying in the wind.
be: Belgium's official flag has an unusual, almost square shape of 13:15, though the longer 2:3 version is the one usually seen on buildings.
bf: Burkina Faso adopted its flag in 1984, along with its new name, which is usually translated as 'land of upright people'.
bg: Bulgaria's white, green and red flag dates from 1879 and is usually described as the Russian tricolor with green in place of blue.
bh: The five white points on Bahrain's flag stand for the Five Pillars of Islam; the number of points was fixed at five in 2002.
bi: The three green-edged red stars on Burundi's flag stand for the national motto: Unity, Work, Progress.
bj: Benin first flew its green, yellow and red flag in 1959, used a green flag with a red star from 1975, and brought the original back in 1990.
bn: The scroll beneath the crest on Brunei's flag reads 'Brunei Darussalam' in Arabic script, meaning 'Brunei, Abode of Peace'.
bo: Bolivia's 2009 constitution made the checkered Wiphala of Andean peoples a national symbol, flown alongside the red, yellow and green tricolor.
br: The stars on Brazil's flag show the sky over Rio de Janeiro on the morning of November 15, 1889, the day the country became a republic.
bs: On the Bahamas flag, aquamarine stands for the sea, gold for the sunny beaches, and the black triangle for the strength of the people.
bt: Bhutan's flag shows Druk, the Thunder Dragon, because the Bhutanese call their country Druk Yul, 'Land of the Thunder Dragon'.
bw: The light blue on Botswana's flag stands for rain, so precious there that 'pula', the word for rain, is also the national motto and the currency.
by: The red-and-white strip at the hoist of Belarus's flag is a traditional embroidery pattern like those on decorated ritual towels called rushniks.
bz: Belize's flag is one of very few national flags to show people: two woodcutters with tools, standing beneath a mahogany tree.
ca: Canada's Maple Leaf flag was first raised on February 15, 1965, and the stylized maple leaf in its center has 11 points.
cd: DR Congo adopted its current sky-blue flag with a red diagonal and yellow star in 2006, reviving a design close to its 1963-1971 flag.
cf: The Central African Republic's flag mixes the French colors with pan-African green and yellow, expressing hope that Europe and Africa could work together.
cg: Congo's diagonal green, yellow and red flag was first used in 1959, replaced by a red flag from 1970, and restored in 1991.
ch: Switzerland's flag is one of only two square national flags in the world; the other belongs to Vatican City.
ci: Ivory Coast's flag is easy to mix up with Ireland's: Ivory Coast puts the orange stripe next to the pole, while Ireland puts green there.
cl: Chile's flag, adopted in 1817, is nicknamed 'La Estrella Solitaria', meaning 'The Lone Star'.
cm: Cameroon's single gold star dates from 1975, when it replaced the two stars that had stood for the country's former eastern and western states.
cn: China's five-star red flag was designed by Zeng Liansong, an economist living in Shanghai, whose entry was picked from about 3,000 in 1949.
co: Colombia's flag is not an even tricolor: the yellow stripe is as tall as the blue and red stripes put together.
cr: Costa Rica's flag got its red stripe in 1848 at the suggestion of Pacífica Fernández, the president's wife, inspired by that year's revolution in France.
cu: Cuba's flag was designed in 1849, more than 50 years before Cuba became an independent republic in 1902.
cv: The circle of ten stars on Cabo Verde's flag stands for the ten main islands of the archipelago.
cy: The map on Cyprus's flag is copper-colored, a nod to the island's ancient copper mines; the word 'copper' itself is linked to the island's name.
cz: The Czech Republic kept the old Czechoslovak flag in 1993, even though the law dividing the country said neither new state should use it.
de: Germany's black, red and gold are traditionally traced to the uniforms of the Lützow Free Corps, volunteers who fought Napoleon in 1813.
dj: Djibouti's flag was first raised at independence in 1977; its light blue stands for the sea and sky, green for the earth, and the red star for unity.
dk: Denmark's Dannebrog is considered the oldest national flag still in use; legend says it fell from the sky during a battle in 1219.
dm: Dominica's flag shows the rare Sisserou parrot, the national bird, making it one of very few national flags that use the color purple.
do: The Dominican Republic's flag is the only national flag with a picture of a Bible, shown open in the middle of its coat of arms.
dz: Algeria's flag became the national flag at independence in 1962; green is often said to stand for Islam and white for peace.
ec: Ecuador's flag looks almost exactly like Colombia's; the easiest way to tell them apart is the coat of arms with a condor in Ecuador's center.
ee: Estonia's blue, black and white flag began as the banner of a student society and was consecrated in Otepää on June 4, 1884.
eg: The golden eagle in the middle of Egypt's flag is known as the Eagle of Saladin, after the famous 12th-century sultan.
er: The olive wreath and branch on Eritrea's flag recall the country's 1952 flag, which showed the same olive emblem on a light blue field.
es: Spain's red and yellow colors were chosen in 1785 by King Charles III so that Spanish ships would be easy to recognize at sea.
et: Ethiopia's green, yellow and red inspired the flags of many African nations, and the blue emblem in its center was added in 1996.
fi: Finland's blue cross is often said to show blue lakes and white snow, an image made popular by the poet Zachris Topelius in the 1800s.
fj: The shield on Fiji's flag shows sugar cane, a coconut palm, bananas and a dove of peace, beneath a lion holding a cocoa pod.
fm: The four white stars on Micronesia's flag stand for its four states: Chuuk, Kosrae, Pohnpei and Yap.
fr: France's tricolor came out of the 1789 Revolution and is traditionally said to join the red and blue of Paris with the white of the monarchy.
ga: The yellow stripe on Gabon's flag stands for the equator, which runs right through the country, as well as for the sun.
gb: The United Kingdom's Union Flag combines the crosses of St George, St Andrew and St Patrick; Wales is not represented on it.
gd: Grenada's flag includes a nutmeg pod, because the island is one of the world's best-known producers of the spice.
ge: Georgia's Five Cross Flag was adopted in 2004, reviving a design based on medieval Georgian banners.
gh: Ghana's flag was designed in 1957 by Theodosia Okoh, and its black star is often called the lodestar of African freedom.
gm: The blue stripe across the middle of Gambia's flag stands for the Gambia River, which runs through the whole country.
gn: Guinea's flag uses the same colors as Mali's but in reverse: Guinea's reads red, yellow, green from the pole, while Mali's reads green, yellow, red.
gq: The six stars on Equatorial Guinea's flag stand for the mainland and the five main islands, shown beneath a silk-cotton tree.
gr: The nine stripes on Greece's flag are often said to match the nine syllables of the Greek motto 'Freedom or Death'.
gt: The quetzal bird on Guatemala's flag stands for liberty, and the scroll beneath it shows the independence date, September 15, 1821.
gw: Guinea-Bissau's flag, with a black star on a red band, is based on the flag of the movement that led the country to independence.
gy: Guyana's flag, nicknamed 'The Golden Arrowhead', was designed by American flag expert Whitney Smith, who coined the word 'vexillology'.
hn: The five stars on Honduras's flag stand for the five nations of the old Federal Republic of Central America and the hope they may unite again.
hr: The red-and-white checkerboard on Croatia's flag is called the šahovnica, and the crown above it holds the arms of five historic regions.
ht: Legend says Haiti's flag was born in 1803 when Jean-Jacques Dessalines tore the white out of a French flag and Catherine Flon sewed the rest together.
hu: Hungary's tricolor became a national symbol in 1848; red is traditionally said to stand for strength, white for faithfulness and green for hope.
id: Indonesia's red-and-white flag looks just like Monaco's; the only real difference is the shape, as Indonesia's flag is longer.
ie: Ireland's tricolor was presented in 1848 by Thomas Francis Meagher; the white in the middle stands for peace between the green and the orange.
il: The blue stripes on Israel's flag are based on the tallit, the traditional Jewish prayer shawl.
in: The wheel on India's flag is the Ashoka Chakra, with 24 spokes, taken from a lion sculpture made for Emperor Ashoka over 2,000 years ago.
iq: The words 'Allahu Akbar' were added to Iraq's flag in 1991, and in 2008 the three green stars that had been on the flag since 1963 were removed.
ir: The phrase 'Allahu Akbar' appears 22 times along the stripes of Iran's flag, recalling the date of the 1979 revolution in the Iranian calendar.
is: Iceland's flag colors are often said to stand for the blue of the sky and sea, the white of ice and snow, and the red of volcanic fire.
it: Italy's tricolor was first adopted as a state flag in 1797 by the Cispadane Republic, which is why January 7 is celebrated as Flag Day.
jm: Jamaica's black, green and gold flag is often said to be the only national flag today with none of the colors red, white or blue.
jo: The seven points of the white star on Jordan's flag stand for the seven verses of Al-Fatiha, the opening chapter of the Quran.
jp: Japan's sun flag, the Hinomaru, has been used for centuries, yet it only became the official national flag by law in 1999.
ke: The shield and two spears on Kenya's flag are based on a traditional Maasai shield and stand for the defense of freedom.
kg: Kyrgyzstan's sun has 40 rays for 40 legendary tribes; in 2023 the rays were made straight so the sun would look less like a sunflower.
kh: Cambodia's flag shows the temple of Angkor Wat, making it one of very few national flags with a building on it.
ki: Kiribati's flag shows a frigatebird over a rising sun with 17 rays, said to stand for the 16 Gilbert Islands plus Banaba.
km: Comoros has used several different national flags since gaining independence in 1975, and its current design was adopted in 2001.
kn: The two white stars on Saint Kitts and Nevis's flag officially stand for hope and liberty, though many people see them as the two islands.
kp: North Korea's flag, adopted in 1948, is called 'Ramhongsaek Konghwagukgi', meaning 'blue and red-colored flag of the republic'.
kr: The four black trigrams on South Korea's Taegeukgi stand for heaven, earth, water and fire, arranged around the red and blue taegeuk circle.
kw: Kuwait's flag was adopted in 1961, and the black shape at its hoist is a trapezoid rather than a triangle.
kz: Kazakhstan's flag, adopted in 1992, shows a steppe eagle under a sun with 32 rays, with a traditional ornament running along the hoist.
la: Laos's flag was first designed in 1945 and became the national flag in 1975; its white disc is often said to be the moon over the Mekong River.
lb: The green tree on Lebanon's flag is the Lebanon cedar, a tree famous since ancient times and mentioned many times in the Bible.
lc: Saint Lucia's flag shows the island's famous Pitons, two volcanic peaks, as black, white and gold triangles on a blue background.
li: Liechtenstein added a gold crown to its flag in 1937 after discovering at the 1936 Olympics that its flag was identical to Haiti's.
lk: The four leaves in the corners of Sri Lanka's flag come from the sacred bo tree, and the lion holding a sword is a symbol going back centuries.
lr: Liberia's flag is modeled on the US flag; its 11 stripes stand for the 11 signers of Liberia's 1847 Declaration of Independence.
ls: Lesotho's flag shows a black mokorotlo, the traditional Basotho straw hat, and was adopted in 2006 for the 40th anniversary of independence.
lt: Lithuania's tricolor dates from 1918; yellow is often said to stand for the sun, green for forests and hope, and red for courage.
lu: Luxembourg's flag looks a lot like the Netherlands' flag, but it is longer and uses a lighter shade of blue.
lv: Latvia's carmine red and white flag is described in a chronicle from the late 1200s, making it one of the oldest flag designs in the world.
ly: From 1977 to 2011 Libya's flag was plain green with no design at all; the current flag revives the one used at independence in 1951.
ma: The green star on Morocco's flag is a pentagram known as the Seal of Solomon, and it was added to the plain red flag in 1915.
mc: Monaco's red and white come from the Grimaldi family, which has ruled since 1297; the flag is nearly identical to Indonesia's but not as long.
md: Moldova's flag looks much like Romania's, but its center shows an eagle bearing a shield with the head of an aurochs, a wild ox.
me: Montenegro's flag, adopted in 2004, is red with a gold border, and its double-headed eagle holds a shield with a golden lion.
mg: Madagascar's flag, adopted in 1958, uses red and white, colors often linked to the Merina kingdom that once ruled much of the island.
mh: The 24 points on the Marshall Islands' star stand for its districts, and the orange and white stripes for the Ralik and Ratak island chains.
mk: North Macedonia's yellow sun with eight rays is often described as 'the new sun of liberty' mentioned in the country's national anthem.
ml: Mali's first flag in 1959 showed a human figure called a kanaga, but it was removed in 1961, leaving plain green, gold and red stripes.
mm: Myanmar adopted its current yellow, green and red flag with a large white star in 2010.
mn: The golden emblem on Mongolia's flag is the Soyombo, a symbol from a script created in 1686 by the Buddhist scholar Zanabazar.
mr: In 2017 Mauritania added red stripes to the top and bottom of its flag to honor those who gave their lives for the country's independence.
mt: Malta's flag carries the George Cross, a British award for bravery that was given to the whole island and its people in 1942.
mu: Mauritius's four stripes stand for the struggle for freedom, the Indian Ocean, the light of independence, and the island's green farmland.
mv: The red border on the Maldives flag recalls the plain red flag the islands used for centuries before the green panel and crescent were added.
mw: Malawi swapped its rising red sun for a full white sun in 2010, but went back to the original design just two years later, in 2012.
mx: The eagle eating a snake on a cactus in Mexico's flag comes from the Aztec legend of how the site of their capital, Tenochtitlan, was chosen.
my: Malaysia's flag, the Jalur Gemilang or 'Stripes of Glory', has 14 stripes and a 14-pointed star for its 13 states plus the federal government.
mz: Mozambique's flag is often called the only national flag with a modern assault rifle: an AK-47 crossed with a hoe on top of an open book.
na: Namibia's flag was adopted at independence in 1990, and its golden sun with 12 triangular rays is said to stand for life and energy.
ne: Niger's flag is often mixed up with India's, but Niger's is almost square and has a plain orange disc instead of a blue wheel.
ng: Nigeria's green-white-green flag was designed in 1959 by student Michael Taiwo Akinkunmi; his original entry also had a red sun, which was removed.
ni: The rainbow in the coat of arms on Nicaragua's flag makes it one of very few national flags that include the color purple.
nl: The Netherlands' flag was once orange, white and blue after William of Orange, but over time the orange stripe was replaced by red.
no: Norway's flag was designed in 1821 by Frederik Meltzer, who put a blue cross on the red and white Danish design.
np: Nepal's flag is the only national flag that is not a rectangle, and its constitution includes step-by-step geometry for drawing it.
nr: Nauru's flag is a map of its location: a yellow line for the Equator and a 12-pointed star just below it, one point for each original tribe.
nz: New Zealand held two referendums in 2015 and 2016 about changing its flag, and voters chose to keep the current design.
om: The emblem on Oman's flag shows a khanjar, a traditional curved dagger, laid over two crossed swords.
pa: Panama's flag was sewn in 1903 by María Ossa de Amador; its blue and red quarters are said to stand for the country's two main political parties.
pe: Legend says Peru's red and white were inspired by flamingos that General José de San Martín saw taking flight when he landed in 1820.
pg: Papua New Guinea's flag, with a bird of paradise and the Southern Cross, was designed in 1971 by Susan Karike, a 15-year-old schoolgirl.
ph: The Philippines flies its flag upside down, with the red stripe on top, to show that the country is in a state of war.
pk: The white stripe on Pakistan's flag stands for the country's religious minorities, while the green part represents its Muslim majority.
pl: Poland's white and red come from its coat of arms, a white eagle on a red shield, and May 2 is celebrated as the national Flag Day.
ps: Palestine's flag is based on the flag of the 1916 Arab Revolt, which also inspired the flags of Jordan and several other Arab states.
pt: The golden armillary sphere on Portugal's flag is an old navigation instrument honoring the Age of Discovery; the flag dates from 1911.
pw: Palau's flag shows a yellow full moon on blue, as the full moon is traditionally seen as the best time for fishing, planting and celebrations.
py: Paraguay's flag is two-sided: the front shows the national coat of arms, while the back shows a different emblem, the treasury seal.
qa: Qatar's maroon and white flag has an unusual 11:28 shape, making it longer for its height than any other national flag.
ro: Romania's flag is almost identical to Chad's; the main difference is that Romania's blue stripe is a slightly lighter shade.
rs: The cross on the shield of Serbia's flag is surrounded by four firesteels, which are often read as four Cyrillic letters 'S'.
ru: Russia's white, blue and red tricolor was first used on ships in the late 1600s and became the national flag again in 1991.
rw: Rwanda adopted its flag in 2001; blue is said to stand for peace, yellow for economic growth, green for prosperity and the golden sun for enlightenment.
sa: Saudi Arabia's flag is never flown at half-mast, because it carries the Shahada, the Islamic declaration of faith.
sb: The five stars on the Solomon Islands' flag first stood for the country's five districts in 1977 and are now usually said to mean its main island groups.
sc: Seychelles' flag has five bands fanning out from the bottom corner by the pole, meant to show a young nation moving into the future.
sd: Sudan's current flag, adopted in 1970, replaced a blue, yellow and green flag that stood for the Nile, the desert and farmland.
se: Sweden's blue and yellow flag is celebrated on June 6, the National Day, which was known as Swedish Flag Day until 1983.
sg: The five stars on Singapore's flag stand for democracy, peace, progress, justice and equality, and the crescent for a young nation on the rise.
si: Slovenia's coat of arms shows Mount Triglav, the country's highest peak, under three gold stars, which helps tell its flag apart from Slovakia's.
sk: Slovakia's coat of arms shows a white double cross on three blue hills, often said to be the Tatra, Fatra and Mátra mountains.
sl: Sierra Leone's flag uses green for farming and the mountains, white for unity and justice, and blue for the natural harbor of Freetown.
sm: The coat of arms on San Marino's flag shows three towers on the peaks of Mount Titano, each topped with an ostrich feather.
sn: Senegal's flag comes from the short-lived Mali Federation; when Senegal left it in 1960, a green star replaced the human figure in the center.
so: Somalia's flag, a white star on light blue, was designed by Mohammed Awale Liban and adopted in 1954, six years before independence.
sr: Suriname's flag was adopted at independence in 1975, and its yellow star is said to stand for unity and a golden future.
ss: South Sudan's flag became a national flag in 2011, when the country became the world's newest independent nation.
st: The two black stars on Sao Tome and Principe's flag stand for the country's two main islands, São Tomé and Príncipe.
sv: El Salvador's coat of arms, in the center of its flag, carries the motto 'Dios, Unión, Libertad', meaning God, Union, Liberty.
sy: In 2025 Syria adopted a green, white and black flag with three red stars, reviving the independence-era design first adopted in 1930.
sz: Eswatini's flag shows a black and white Nguni shield with two spears and a staff decorated with tassels of bird feathers.
td: Chad's flag is nearly identical to Romania's; the only real difference is that Chad's blue stripe is a slightly darker shade.
tg: Togo's flag was designed by artist Paul Ahyi, who is said to have based its proportions on the golden ratio, about 1 to 1.618.
th: Thailand's flag, the Trairanga or 'tricolor', was adopted in 1917; its red, white and blue are said to stand for nation, religion and king.
tj: Tajikistan's flag shows a crown under an arc of seven stars; seven is often described as a lucky or sacred number in Tajik tradition.
tl: East Timor's flag was raised at independence on May 20, 2002, when the country became the first new sovereign state of the 21st century.
tm: Turkmenistan's flag has five carpet patterns called guls, and in 1997 olive branches were added to honor the country's neutrality.
tn: Tunisia's crescent-and-star flag was introduced by Hussein II Bey around 1827-1831, making it one of the oldest flags in the Arab world.
to: Tonga's constitution says its flag, red with a red cross on a white square, must never be changed.
tr: Turkey's flag is nicknamed 'Al Bayrak', meaning 'the red flag', and its exact shape and proportions were set by a law passed in 1936.
tt: On Trinidad and Tobago's flag, red stands for the warmth of the sun, white for the sea, and the black band for the dedication of the people.
tv: Tuvalu's flag has nine stars for its nine islands, even though the name Tuvalu means 'eight standing together'.
tw: Taiwan's flag is known as 'Blue Sky, White Sun, and a Wholly Red Earth', and its sun has 12 rays said to stand for the 12 months.
tz: Tanzania's flag combines the green of Tanganyika's flag with the blue of Zanzibar's, marking their union in 1964.
ua: Ukraine's blue and yellow flag is popularly said to show a blue sky over golden wheat fields, fitting for a major grain producer.
ug: The grey crowned crane on Uganda's flag stands with one leg raised, a pose said to show the country moving forward.
us: The 50-star flag of the United States has flown since July 4, 1960, longer than any earlier version of the Stars and Stripes.
uy: The nine stripes on Uruguay's flag stand for the country's nine original departments, and the Sun of May shines in the corner.
uz: The 12 stars on Uzbekistan's flag are often said to stand for the 12 months of the year or the 12 signs of the zodiac.
va: Vatican City's square flag shows the crossed keys of Saint Peter, one gold and one silver, beneath the papal tiara.
vc: The three green diamonds on St Vincent's flag form a V for Vincent and are said to show the islands as 'the Gems of the Antilles'.
ve: Venezuela added an eighth star to its flag in 2006, honoring the province of Guayana as Simón Bolívar had decreed in 1817.
vn: The five points of the yellow star on Vietnam's flag are said to stand for farmers, workers, intellectuals, youth and soldiers.
vu: Vanuatu's flag shows a curled pig's tusk, a symbol of prosperity, crossed by two namele leaves that stand for peace.
ws: Samoa's flag shows the Southern Cross with five stars, one much smaller than the others; the design was adopted in 1949.
xk: Kosovo's flag, adopted in 2008, shows a gold map of the country under six white stars, making it one of very few flags with a map.
ye: Yemen's red, white and black flag was adopted in 1990, when North and South Yemen joined together into one country.
za: South Africa's flag was designed in just a few weeks by state herald Frederick Brownell and was first flown in 1994.
zm: Zambia's flag puts its eagle and stripes at the far edge away from the pole; the eagle is said to stand for rising above the nation's problems.
zw: The bird on Zimbabwe's flag is based on soapstone carvings found at Great Zimbabwe, the ancient stone city that gave the country its name.
